name.ja: アーチボルド・スコット・クーパー

overview.en: Archibald Scott Couper was a Scottish chemist who proposed that carbon atoms can link to each other to form chains, independently of Kekulé, laying groundwork for structural chemistry.

early_life.en: Couper was born in Kirkintilloch, Scotland. He studied philosophy and languages before turning to chemistry, working with Charles Adolphe Wurtz in Paris.

impact.en: Couper's theory of carbon self-linking and his use of lines to represent bonds were foundational contributions to structural organic chemistry, though he received less recognition than Kekulé.

event.en: Published 'On a New Chemical Theory' proposing carbon chains
Suffered mental breakdown, ending his career

description.en: Paper proposing that carbon atoms bond to each other in chains

text.en: The art of the chemist consists in making the right experiments.
